barriers_note: T-3554: a `barrier` is what a house model builds outside its footprint between a knee and a head over the ground (tools/prairie_barriers.py): plan rectangles of its cells, `rects` four integers each (i0 i1 j0 j1, half-open), cell (i, j) centred on u0 + i*cell, v0 + j*cell of the model's plan (u = x, v = -z), turned into local E/N by the placement. `barriers` carries them for the built Prairie houses no day goes into.
floors_note: The owner, 2026-11-14 ("Anywhere there are stairs I should be able to climb"): a `floor` is the tops a house model builds outside its walls that a visitor climbs, its stoop's treads and landing and its porches (tools/prairie_barriers.py floor): `rects`, plan rectangles of one height, five integers each (i0 i1 j0 j1 half-open, then the top in centimetres over the model's ground), and `walls`, the same for the rails and cheeks beside them, standing past any step. house-floors.js lays them as walker decks.
stoops_note: T-3554 (owner, 2026-11-13: "no one should be able to" stand in stairs): the stairs no house model carries, as `barriers` rows of one box each (derive_doors_scene.py stoop_rows; `what` says which): the back yards' stoops.
